title: Annual linear fits show a lower combined rain response in 156 mainland south-east Australian catchments after 1996
abstract: We test whether the lower response to current-year rain was balanced by a higher response to prior-year rain. We refit both annual rain coefficients in 1951-1996 and 1997-2021 at 156 mainland south-east Australian catchments. The mean coefficient sum fell by 29.7% with AGCD rain (joint spatial and shared-year 95% limits -43.6 to -15.3%) and 24.9% with SILO (-40.1 to -10.3%). The prior-rain coefficient did not rise at the point estimate. Thus a one-year timing transfer does not account for the full change in the main linear representation. Temperature controls and one- and five-year blocks retained negative sum intervals. With squared current rain, the SILO sum change was smaller and uncertain (-15.1%, -26.8 to +2.8%). Late-period and earlier-control tests were less clear. This is a diagnostic on reused observations, not a physical storage or water-loss estimate. Longer memory, climate variables absent from the regression, catchment change and measurement error remain open. Code, source hashes, coefficients, aggregate draws, a numerical audit and a static figure are supplied.

display.caption: Changes of the current-rain coefficient, prior-rain coefficient and their sum. All changes use the same reference-sum denominator. Bars are joint spatial-cell and shared three-year-block 95% intervals.
